1. Every device, with a suggested short id (like fw-01, core-sw-01). Repeated devices are listed one per line with their own ids - eight identical floor switches are eight lines, never "switches x8" and never one example standing in for the rest.
2. Every connection between devices, including any interface or port names written on the line (like FA0/0, GE0/7, Port 4).
3. The trust areas: what is inside the organization, what is outside.
4. Per-device details, exactly as written: model, addresses, software versions, licenses and their dates, SSIDs, port counts used and available, DHCP or static.
5. Anything dated, expired, or end-of-life - old licenses, unsupported operating systems, aged hardware.
Do not write any code yet - I will paste build instructions next.

This is a short hardware code, never a filename. Use "generic" for hardware with
no artwork of its own. An unlisted code still draws the device at the right
height as a plain labelled face, and marks the saved file with a red FAIL badge
until it is corrected. A face code ending in -1u, -2u, -3u or -4u draws exactly
that many units and must match the device's height: a 1U device cannot use
generic-server-2u.

NEVER TOUCH THESE

- brand - the company logo and name. logoPath is SVG path data. Copy the whole
  brand object through exactly as you found it, character for character. One
  altered character destroys the logo.
- evidence.color must be one of: purple, red, green, amber, teal.
- footer.caveat and footer.redaction are mandatory. Never drop them, and never
  empty them.
- sections.findings.items must never be empty. A document that renders perfectly
  while hiding what it does not know is worse than no document. If you know of
  no gaps, say what has not been verified.

POINTING A GAP AT THE DRAWING

A finding may name what it is about:
  { "title": "...", "detail": "...", "at": "core-sw-01" }
  { "title": "...", "detail": "...", "at": ["access-sw-01", "access-sw-02"] }
  { "title": "...", "detail": "...", "atZone": "perimeter" }

- "at" is a device id, or a list of them. "atZone" is an area id.
- Every id must already exist. A marker pointing at something that does not
  exist is an error.
- Never write the marker number yourself: it comes from the order of the list.
- Leave both out for a finding that is not about one place on the drawing.

SHAPE - keep every field that is already present. Do not rename fields and do
not invent new ones. Fields you may see but must never add yourself: iconAsset
on a node, via on a link. If one is already there, copy it through unchanged.
label, labelX and labelY on a link are optional; if a link already has them keep
them exactly, and do not add labelX/labelY to a new link.

NUMBERS
- A node's x,y is the CENTRE of a box that is 176 wide and 104 tall.
- A zone's x,y is its TOP-LEFT corner.
- The canvas is 1280 x 930. Keep every node centre between x 88 and 1192, and y 52 and 878, or part of the device hangs off the page. If you raise the canvas height, these limits grow with it.
- Construct positions, never estimate them. Inside each area, place node
  centres on a grid: 200 apart across, 140 apart down, the first centre 110
  from the area's left edge and 80 below its top edge. Grid positions never
  overlap and never straddle an edge.
- Size each area for what it holds, before placing: width at least its
  columns x 200 + 20, height at least its rows x 140 + 20.
- If the areas will not fit, raise topology.canvas.height - 48 x the device
  count is a safe height, and the page scrolls. Never tighten the grid to
  make things fit.
- The grid never justifies dropping a device. Every device in the inventory
  goes on the page; when they will not fit, the canvas grows until they do.
- A device must sit FULLY inside an area or fully outside it. One drawn half in
  and half out leaves the reader unable to tell which area it belongs to.
- Two nodes overlap only when their x values are less than 176 apart AND
  their y values are less than 104 apart. Both conditions must be true.
  Nodes far apart vertically may share an x.
- Rack units are numbered from the BOTTOM. position is the lowest unit the
  device fills, so "position": 30 with "height": 2 fills U30 AND U31.
- Every rack device must fit: position >= 1 and position + height - 1 <= units.
- position and height must be numbers, never strings.
- A device that appears both in the topology and in the rack uses the SAME id in
  both places.

TEXT
- Straight quotes only. Never use curly quotes.
- Never use < or > inside any value.
- Every id must be unique, and every link's from and to must name a node id that
  exists.
